CORAM: HON'BLE MR JUSTICE T.G. SHIVASHANKARE GOWDA
ORAL JUDGMENT

In this appeal, the petitioners are seeking enhancement of compensation and also questioning the fastening of the liability against the owner of the motor cycle to pay compensation.
2.
For the sake of convenience, the rank of the parties shall be referred to as per their status before the Tribunal.

3. Brief facts of the case are, on 02.11.2012 at 9.30 p.m., the husband of the first petitioner, father of petitioner Nos.2 to 8 and son of petitioner Nos.9 and 10 by name Narasappa, the deceased, while crossing the Varthur Main Road in front of Bar and Restaurant at Siddapura village, Bengaluru,
motor cycle bearing No.KA-03/HC-231 dashed against him due to which he fell down and sustained injury.
When he was brought to Yashomati Hospital, he was declared brought dead.
NC: 2024:KHC:32397 The petitioners being the wife, children and parents have approached the Tribunal for grant of compensation of Rs.20,00,000/-.
The claim was opposed by the Insurance Company.

After taking the evidence and hearing both parties, the Tribunal awarded compensation of Rs.13,23,320/- with interest @ 6% per annum and fastened the liability against the owner of the motor cycle on the ground that the rider of the motor cycle was holding invalid driving licence.
Aggrieved by the same, the petitioners are before this Court on various heads.

4. Heard the arguments of Sri.K.V.Girish, learned counsel for the petitioners and Sri.A.N.Krishnaswamy, learned counsel for the Insurance Company.
5.

It is contended by the learned counsel for the petitioners that the accident is of the year 2012, the deceased was earning Rs.12,000/- per month, but the Tribunal has taken the income at Rs.6,000/-,
the NC: 2024:KHC:32397 compensation awarded under the conventional heads is on the lower side,
the driving licence is placed before the Court as per Ex.R2 to show that the rider of the motor cycle was holding valid driving licence, but the Tribunal erroneously held that it is invalid driving licence and sought for direction to the Insurance Company to pay the compensation.
6.

Per contra, learned counsel for the Insurance company has contended that the evidence is placed before the Tribunal explaining that the driving licence relied upon by the petitioners is not a valid driving licence, the ARTO Farooqabad (Fatehgarh) has issued Ex.R2/driving licence to show that the driving licence is not valid as no driving licence fee was paid and thereby it is an invalid driving licence.

When the rider was holding an invalid driving licence, it is not proper on the part of the petitioners to ask the Insurance Company to pay compensation, the Insurance Company can avoid Smt. Lalithamma vs M/S Bajaj Allianz General Insurance Co ...

its liability, the Tribunal has rightly NC: 2024:KHC:32397 fastened the liability against the owner of the motorcycle and the compensation assessed by the Tribunal is proportionate to the income of the deceased and it is not a case for enhancement.
7. I have given my anxious consideration to the arguments addressed on behalf of both sides and also perused the materials on record.

8. The material on record shows that on 02.11.2012 at 9:30 p.m. while the deceased was crossing the road at Siddapura village on Varthur Main Road, he was hit by a motorcycle due to which he sustained injury, during transit to the hospital, he succumbed to death.

Petitioner No.1 is the wife,
petitioner No.2 is the daughter, petitioner Nos.3 to 8 are minor children of the deceased to the first petitioner and petitioner Nos.9 and 10 are the parents of the deceased.
The postmortem report points out that the deceased was aged 45 years on the date of accident.
The Tribunal has taken income at NC: 2024:KHC:32397 Rs.6,000/-; the petitioners being dependents on the deceased are entitled to claim compensation.

9. In a case of this nature, compensation has to be determined by following the principles settled by the Hon'ble Apex Court in National Insurance Co.Ltd. -vs- Pranay Sethi and Others1, Sarla Varma (Smt.) and Others -vs- Delhi Transport Corporation and Another2 and Magma General Insurance Co.Ltd. -vs- Nanu Ram @ Chuhru Ram and Others3.
10.

sentences.text: Though the petitioners are claiming that the deceased was earning Rs.12,000/- per month, there is no proof of income.
The Tribunal treated the deceased as a person with no proof of income and taken income at Rs.6,000/- per month.
In the year 2012, a person with no proof of income will earn not less than Rs.7,000/-.
Hence, notional income of the deceased (2017) 16 SCC 680 (2009) 6 SCC 121 (2018) 18 SCC 130 NC: 2024:KHC:32397 has to be taken at Rs.7,000/-.
Since the deceased was aged less than 50 years, 25% has to be added as future prospects.

There are 10 dependents, hence,
1/5th has to be deducted towards personal expenses.

Then the loss of dependency will be:
Rs.7,000/- + 1,750/- (25%) = Rs.8,750/- - Rs.1,750/- (1/5 th) = Rs.7,000/-x12x14 = Rs.11,76,000/-.
The deceased left behind his wife, seven children and parents.
Loss of Consortium to wife and loss of love and affection to the children and parents at Rs.40,000/- each has to be considered; funeral expenses at Rs.15,000/- and loss of estate at Rs.15,000/-.
In view of judgment in Pranay Sethi's case, since the accident is of the year 2012, 10% appreciation on the conventional heads has to be given.
Then the compensation under conventional heads comes to Rs.4,73,000/-, thereby the total compensation comes to Rs.16,49,000/- as against Rs.13,23,320/- awarded by the Tribunal.

Thus,
petitioners are entitled for enhancement of Rs.3,25,680/-, it is the just compensation to which the NC: 2024:KHC:32397 petitioners are entitled, in the facts and circumstances of the case.
11. As regarding liability is concerned, the Tribunal has discussed that the rider of the motorcycle was holding invalid driving licence.

In a case where a person holding invalid driving licence, the Hon'ble Apex Court in Parminder Singh -vs- New India Assurance Co.Ltd. and Others at para 7 held as follows:

sentences.text: " 7. On the issue of liability to pay the compensation awarded, we affirm the view taken by the High Court that the Respondent - Insurance Company is absolved of the liability to bear the compensation, as evidence has been produced from the office of the Regional Transport Office to prove that the drivers of the two offending trucks were driving on the basis of invalid driving licenses.
It is also relevant to note that the owners and drivers of the offending trucks have not appeared at any stage of the proceedings, including this Court."
It is pertinent to note that the facts of the above case is identical to the facts of the case on hand.

Under such circumstances, the finding of the Tribunal that the - 10 - NC: 2024:KHC:32397 owner has to pay the compensation is proper and Insurance Company can avoid its liability, but the circumstances necessitate application of principle of 'Pay and Recovery'.
Hence, the Insurance Company has to pay the compensation and recover it from the owner of the motorcycle.

(iv) The Insurance Company is directed to deposit the entire compensation amount with interest @ 6% within eight weeks from the date of receipt of certified copy - 11 - NC: 2024:KHC:32397 of this judgment and recover the same from the owner of the motor cycle in the same proceedings;
(vi) The amount in deposit, if any, shall be transmitted to the Tribunal along with records.
